newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen shares end noon easier on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end noon easier on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices fell at midday on Tuesday, pressured by profit-taking after recent rebounds, brokers said.
The hard currency B share index lost 1.87 points or 1.39 percent to 132.38 points on turnover of HK$22 million.
The domestic A share index shed 1.88 points or 0.46 percent to 409.13 points on turnover of 3.5 billion yuan.
"The B share market's strong rebound in the past three sessions triggered profit-taking (this morning)," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
"The B share index needs a correction before picking up again," said a stock trader at Hainan Province Trust and Investment Co in Shenzhen.

Slight optimism over listed firms' 1997 interim results and the government's stock market policy were likely to cap losses, brokers said, with one adding that he saw limited downsides for both indicies in Tuesday afternoon trading.
Slower listings of new A shares recently had resulted in some funds being diverted from the primary market, brokers said. A shares had been seen as one of the main engines powering the recent rally.

Brokers have said that Beijing has been slowing the pace of market expansion since early July on the belief that a string of anti-speculation measures launched in May and June had effectively cooled the markets.
In the B share market, Chengming Paper was the most actively traded issue on volume of 1.14 million shares, sinking HK$0.15 to HK$7.55 on profit-taking, brokers said.

Colour television maker Shenzhen Huafa Electronics was the biggest A share loser, falling 0.55 yuan or 5.41 percent to 9.62 yuan as investors expected poor interim results from the company, they said.
